# cfg_gen.py input for KuRALSNetNPUSeg, 8x64 SoC buffer (8 Doppler x 64 Range).
# GENERATED by kurals/manifest_to_cfg_input.py from kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_int8_manifest.json
# (this directory) -- do not hand-edit; regenerate if the checkpoint changes.
# 
# Source checkpoint: checkpoints/8x64_maxpool_0.6122_bc64/results/test_doppler_model.pt
#   val dice 0.6122 / test dice 0.6749, epoch 220.
#   stem_stride=1, encoder_depth=1, eltwise_act=linear, bottleneck_ch=64,
#   bottleneck_kernel_size=3, leaky slope 0.125, w_eff=2*w_stored+1,
#   down1.downsample='maxpool' (see below).
# 
# NPU-legal on two axes, both hardware constraints and both guarded in code:
#  1. Eltwise-add activation. The three [shortcut] blocks carry activation=linear --
#     an eltwise-add on this hardware has no usable activation stage of its own; a
#     conv must follow to supply the nonlinearity. Guarded by export_int8.py's
#     LEGAL_ELTWISE_ACTS and this generator. See CLAUDE.md's 'Eltwise-add activation'.
#  2. Row-reuse/frame-reuse dataflow. See the CUTPOINT block below -- this is the
#     first checkpoint in this repo built to satisfy it; every earlier "NPU-legal"
#     8x64 checkpoint (including 8x64_eltwiselinear_0.6328_bc64) also used a strided
#     depthwise conv for down1, which is illegal once CUTPOINT<=3 forces down1 into
#     the frame-reuse domain -- retroactively not deployable either. See
#     CLAUDE.md's "Row-reuse vs frame-reuse grouping" and checkpoints/README.md.
# 
# bias_shift/act_shift are that checkpoint's own calibrated shift2/shift1 -- inputs
# to cfg_gen.py, not something it derives (same as the reference tiny_yolov2 input).
# Valid for this exact checkpoint only.
# 
# Resolution ladder is {8x64, 4x32} only -- no 2x16 activation anywhere. head_out
# predicts per-pixel at 8x64, so there is no final upsample (manifest
# final_upsample=1); argmax decode still happens off-NPU.
# 
# Verified on Test via benchmark_int8_pipeline.py's pure-integer replay (the actual
# deployed arithmetic): Acc=0.9987 Prec=0.8641 Pd=0.7679 FAR=0.0007 mDice=0.8736.
# Below the retroactively-illegal 0.6328 checkpoint's 0.8906 -- the maxpool fix
# below (a fused maxpool instead of a learned stride-2 depthwise conv for down1)
# appears to cost a modest amount of accuracy; not chased further this round, see
# checkpoints/README.md.
# 
# Companion files here: sample_ifm_64x8.npy is one real recorded frame;
# sample_ifm_64x8.int8.npy is that frame quantized with THIS manifest's input_scale
# (0.000637315) -- the literal bytes the first conv consumes. Regenerate it with
# quantize_input.py if the checkpoint changes; the scale is checkpoint-specific.
# 
# cfg_gen.py settings: INPUT_FILE="input/kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64.txt", WIDTH=64,
# HEIGHT=8, CUTPOINT=3 (npu_idx 0-2 -- stem.dw, stem.pw, stageA.dw -- row-reuse;
# npu_idx 3 onward -- stageA.pw through head_out -- frame-reuse). Hard hardware
# rules (confirmed 2026-09-11): the row-reuse -> frame-reuse transition can happen
# at most once, [route] is only legal inside the frame-reuse domain, [shortcut] may
# never cross the transition at all, and a strided depthwise conv is illegal inside
# the frame-reuse domain. Given those rules:
#  - The dec_a route (stageA.pw npu_idx 3, upconv_a.pw npu_idx 19, consumer
#    dec_a.dw npu_idx 20) requires the *earliest* of those -- stageA.pw -- to
#    already be in the frame-reuse domain. Since the transition is a single
#    monotonic threshold, that forces CUTPOINT <= 3.
#  - CUTPOINT=3 is the latest value satisfying that (keeps the most layers in
#    row-reuse). All three bottleneck shortcuts (pairs at npu_idx 7/9, 9/11,
#    11/13) land entirely inside the resulting frame-reuse region -- no
#    crossing, no extra care needed.
#  - down1.dw (npu_idx 4, stride 2) unavoidably lands in the frame-reuse domain
#    too (same reason as above -- no CUTPOINT choice exempts it without also
#    breaking the route rule), so it can no longer be a strided depthwise conv.
#    KuRALSNetNPUSeg now builds it as a stride-1 depthwise conv followed by a
#    fused maxpool(k=2) -- see kurals/models/quant.py's QuantDepthwiseSeparableBlock
#    docstring -- hence the [maxpool] section right after down1_dw below.
# This second rule did require an architecture change and a retrain, unlike the
# plain CUTPOINT choice, since it changes the actual computation (a strided conv
# and stride-1-then-maxpool are different functions even though down1's depthwise
# weight shape is unchanged). Verified by running cfg_gen.py with these settings:
# stageA_pw is tagged `cutlayer`, down1_dw is tagged `maxpool`, dec_a_dw is tagged
# `concat`, head_out keeps `last_layer`, and Buffer1/Buffer2 both come to 32768
# Bytes -- under buf_size=0x12200 (74240B) with room to spare.
# 
# 'from'/'layers' are raw 0-based indices into this file's own section list (how
# cfg_gen.py indexes cfg[], counting non-conv sections), NOT Darknet's negative
# relative offsets.
# 
# UNRESOLVED before trusting a generated npu_cfg.c against real silicon:
#  1. PF=16 channel alignment. dec_a_pw (24 ch) and head_out (4 ch) are not
#     multiples of PF, so cfg_gen.py silently rounds them up (24->32, 4->16) for
#     its buffer/address math but does NOT pad the actual weights. Those two
#     layers need explicit zero-padded weight export, and head_out's consumer must
#     read only the first 4 channels.
#  2. First-layer channels. cfg_gen.py hardcodes CHANNEL=PF=16 for every workload
#     (including 3-channel RGB ones), while this model's input is 1 channel. If
#     that reflects a real fixed DMA width, stem weights need the same zero-pad.
#  3. upconv_a_pw's output scale is forced onto stageA_pw's grid for the concat
#     (the hardware concat has no rescale). The register format has no field for
#     that; export_int8.py already applies it when deriving this layer's
#     scale/shift/bias, so do not recompute those independently.
